title: Epic: Advanced Craft — routes, constraints, reharmonization, and practice
description:
## Background
This milestone composes the same trusted laws/corpus/time/voice services into the ambitious Harmonic Discovery workbenches selected by the focused Idea Wizard.

## Goals
- Progression-level voicing, MIDI, route search, constraint harmonization, proof-carrying branches.
- Guide-tone and contextual color work, cadence/rhythm/tension transforms.
- Motif/sequence and honest nonfunctional/common-tone transforms.
- Deterministic chart-to-practice engine and all discovery/workbench UI.
- Curated lessons, prompts, help, and full mobile workflows.

## Included plan packages
V2, E1, G3-G9, U6, U7, U9-U11, D1.

## Guardrails
Search uses deterministic state/work-quanta/memory caps and cooperative yielding; wall time never changes musical output. Preview/search/branches are nonmutating. Every Apply is one exact-timing revision-checked command. No hidden worker, model, or network dependency.

## Epic exit
All fifteen Idea Wizard capabilities are usable and individually traceable to conformance/E2E/limit/evidence artifacts; MIDI and every advanced workflow preserve the core musical/data/audio invariants.

title: V2: Bounded progression voicing optimizer
description:
## Background
Reviewed package V2 turns event-local legal voicings into a deterministic progression-level realization service shared by playback, MIDI, constraints, and the voice-leading workbench.

## Required implementation
Implement the resumable optimizer over V1 motion/cost vectors and V0 candidates. Respect Manual/Frozen event boundaries, locks, bass/range/family constraints, exact source event IDs, 96 raw and 24 retained candidates per event, beam width 48, and a 512-event chart cap. Return Pareto alternatives, selected realization IDs, degradation/conflict explanations, SearchStats, and explicit termination.

## Determinism and bounds
Search advances only by fixed work quanta with stable ordering/tie-breaks and cooperative yielding; wall-clock time is measurement, never a semantic cutoff. Enforce state/memory/work-quanta caps and distinguish complete, exhausted, cancelled, and work-quanta-cap results. Never mutate the document or silently relax a hard constraint.

## Success criteria
Identical input/version/profile yields byte-identical alternatives across yield schedules. Small cases equal exhaustive brute force. Manual/Frozen pitches survive exactly, boundaries are honored, and every degraded/no-result outcome names the responsible constraints.

## Test and evidence
Add brute-force oracle tests, seeded/metamorphic determinism, 96/24/48/512 bound cases, cancellation/resume/yield-schedule equivalence, impossible locks/ranges, Manual/Frozen seams, Pareto dominance, memory/work counters, and performance observations at 100 ms interactive and 500 ms large-chart targets without using those clocks to select output.

## Non-goals
No stochastic model, hidden relaxation, factorial assignment, UI, audio scheduling, or MIDI byte writing.
close_reason: V2 package epic complete (2026-07-23, VioletMill): all three phases closed with green gates. V2/spec (ulj.1.1): contract doc + frozen types + 47-case independent fixture authority + validator with reference beam and brute force, 27 mutation controls all caught; amendment #1 (content-memoization law) recorded. V2/build (ulj.1.2): production src/theory/progression-optimizer.ts — pure unit-resumable stepper, exact counter semantics, windows/segments/loop closure, V1 oracle binding with content cache; 96 tests (unit + real-V1 integration + performance observation). V2/verify (ulj.1.3): hash-bound evidence gate verify:v2-evidence — clean-invocation suite rerun, 40-seed metamorphic conformance vs independent exhaustive fold, drift-checked closure, ledger under test-results/v2-evidence/. Downstream consumers (G4 workbench, E1 MIDI export, U6 voice-leading workbench) can now build on the public V2 contract. Follow-up: jcpe-72iu tracks the V1 per-call cost that bounds the release performance gate.

title: U6: Progression voice-leading workbench
description:
## Background
This is reviewed plan package U6 in the Advanced Craft milestone and completes a user-facing portion of the deterministic product contract.

## Required implementation
Expose V2 with current/alternative realization lanes, exact pitches/roles, motion and cost axes, bass/guide summaries, Manual/Frozen boundaries, locks, family/range/bass controls, Pareto/degradation/conflict/search status, keyboard/touch selection, exact per-event audition via X1, ephemeral A/B and one revision-checked freeze/Apply command.

## Invariants and risks
Search never edits while running; audition never changes document selection or playhead; Manual pitches are immutable; wall-time display never changes results; every visual has labels and nonvisual equivalents.

## Success criteria
Users can understand changes, lock/freeze, compare/cancel/resume, hear exact pitches and Apply/Undo with stable timing/identity at mobile and 200 percent zoom.

## Test plan and detailed logging
E2E audition, lock/freeze, Manual seams, Pareto selection, cancellation/resume, stale Apply, A/B/global Stop/Undo; keyboard/screen-reader, focus, 320px/forced colors/reduced motion, exact pitch and leak logs.

## Non-goals
No notation engraving, drag-only pitch editing, or UI-owned voicing algorithm. Preserve unrelated work.

No packet files written yet; the complete reconnaissance and design are banked below so the next claimant (or my later session) starts warm. E1 (upstream) is fully closed; the P0/E1 join caveat is jcpe-u0mc.

# U7/spec design sketch (pre-mapper draft)

## Placement
- Contract module: `src/application/u7-midi-export-workflow-contract.ts` (application may
  import export/playback/domain; UI may not import export, so the workflow contract that
  references E1 report/loss types must live in application; the UI half is expressed as
  view-model types the future dialog renders). Imported by nothing in production
  (proposed packet — same status as the A0-E0 bridge).
- Doc: `docs/U7_MIDI_EXPORT_WORKFLOW_CONTRACT.md`
- Fixtures: `tests/fixtures/midi-export-workflow/` — manifest, preview-cases,
  state-cases, limit-cases, mutation-controls, trace-ledger, provenance-ledger.
- Validator: `scripts/validate-u7-contract.ts` (no src imports, restates constants,
  independently re-derives preview models; hash expectations computed from E1's pinned
  golden bytesHex so production is never consulted).
- Static test: `tests/static/u7-contract.test.ts`.

## Key laws to freeze
1. Preview binding: (documentId, revision) pinned at open; every later stage re-checks;
   stale → `u7.revision_stale`, never silent re-read.
2. Preview model: readiness; realization summary (generated/manual/frozen counts);
   PPQ 960 / tempo / meter / 2 tracks; bass policy disclosure (V0 external bass
   excluded exactly as declared); blocked events (voicing failures + E1 refusals incl.
   jcpe-u0mc duplicate-unison, linked, capped at MAX_DOCUMENT_CHORD_EVENTS);
   losses (E1 three kinds + U7 notice kinds); safe filename (E1 law);
   deterministic artifact hash sha256 lowercase hex over SMF bytes; byteLength.
3. Marker derivation law (U7-owned, E1 never derives text):
   - chord markers: canonical T0 symbol per event, source order;
   - section markers: section name per section-start event;
   - text > 96 UTF-8 bytes or containing control chars → marker OMITTED, event listed
     in preview as omitted-annotation (reason: text-over-limit / text-control-chars) —
     disclosed omission, never truncation, never blocking.
   - title: empty → "Untitled"; >96 bytes → code-point-safe byte truncation WITH a
     preview notice (track-name metadata, not musical data; disclosed).
   - voicingTrackName "Voicings", instrumentName pinned literal.
4. Generate: exportMidi on the compiled current-revision plan; any E1 refusal surfaces
   as a blocked preview (u7.export_refused carrying the E1 code); no partial bytes.
5. Delivery: single-use capacity-one prepared registry (mirrors canonical-export
   discipline, restated); synchronous activation start; object-URL cleanup laws
   restated from accepted E0 (structural equality pinned by static test, E0 v1 pins
   unchanged — additive idiom); MIDI delivery binding kind "standard-midi-file";
   MIDI export NEVER touches the canonical lastExport marker and NEVER calls recovery
   Save; cancellation/failure advances nothing.
6. Dialog state machine (closed set): idle → preview-open → generating → ready →
   delivering → delivered; cancel/close from every non-delivering state; stale detected
   at generate and at delivery-take; failure states with cleanup outcomes; re-preview
   from stale. Focus/live-region matrix per state (open focus target, announcement
   text keys, Escape behavior, focus return on close).
7. Accessibility state matrix: per state × surface (dialog ≥768px / sheet <768px):
   initial focus, live-region politeness+key, allowed actions, focus-return-on-close.
8. Work bounds: preview assembly counters (events visited, markers derived, bytes
   hashed) with limits from P0/E1 caps.

## Refusal codes (precedence order, draft)
u7.request_invalid, u7.document_unavailable, u7.revision_stale,
u7.realization_blocked, u7.plan_refused, u7.export_refused, u7.hash_unavailable,
u7.preparation_conflict, u7.preparation_missing, u7.delivery_not_prepared?,
limit.u7_preview_work_exceeded.
(Delivery failures are outcomes, not refusals — E0 idiom.)

## Fixture case families
- PRE (preview): clean chart (bind E1-GLD-001 bytes/hash), losses chart (GLD-005/006),
  blocked voicing, duplicate-unison blocked (jcpe-u0mc citation), omitted long symbol,
  omitted control-char section name, truncated long title, external bass disclosure,
  empty title → Untitled, loop chart.
- STA (state machine): full happy path; cancel at preview/ready; close at each;
  stale at generate; stale at take; delivery cancelled; delivery failed;
  cleanup-failed; single-use second-take refused; re-preview after stale.
- LIM: 96/97-byte marker text boundary; title truncation boundary; blocked list cap;
  preparation id bounds; state-matrix completeness.
- MUT: pointer corruptions (~16).
- Trace: every bead requirement row → cases + named future owners
  (tests/unit/u7-*.test.ts, e2e owner naming per U0/U1 precedent).
- Provenance: SMF/E1 authority, accepted E0 v1 pins, U0 a11y matrix authority,
  expectedValuesGenerated false.

RECON ADDENDA (from the surface-mapping pass): U1 packet = the template (7 fixtures incl root w/ companionSha256, validator with 36 U7_CONTRACT_*-style finding codes, --allow-pending-freeze, static test with negative tmpdir controls). A0 has 16 command kinds / 12 ephemeral intents; mark-exported exists and must be explicitly NOT claimed by U7 (MIDI is lossy, never advances exportRevision). APPLICATION_DIALOG_KINDS (6) needs a proposed 7th 'midi-export' via additive superset tuple. No A0 request kind needed (preview is sync; delivery uses prepared-registry discipline: E0 PREPARED_CANONICAL_EXPORT_REGISTRY_STATES = empty/preparing/ready/delivering). ui may NOT import export => contract module lives in src/application/u7-midi-export-workflow-contract.ts. Delivery v1 freezes object-url-download only (FSA deferred). Hash: NEW branded raw-bytes sha256 lowercase hex (E0's SemanticDocumentHash hashes canonical JSON, not artifact bytes; A1 RecoveryExportBinding.artifactSha256 is the byte-hash precedent). Blocked-events preview needs a U7-owned full-walk assembly (buildStudioRealizations stops at first refusal). Title/section/symbol texts can reach 256 code points vs E1's 96-byte marker law => omit-and-disclose for markers, code-point-safe truncation + notice for title, literal 'Untitled' for empty. Overlay: sheet is the only kind legal in both modal modes; breakpoint 640 (U0 compactBreakpointCssPx). Gate id u7-midi-export-workflow-contract after e1-midi-export-contract in scripts/verify.ts; also add the missing E1 + new U7 packet-registration bullets in ARCHITECTURE.md.

This is reviewed plan package U7 in the Advanced Craft milestone and completes a user-facing portion of the deterministic product contract.

## Background
This is reviewed plan package E1 in the Advanced Craft milestone and implements a selected deterministic Idea Wizard capability.

Consume the shared playback plan; never reparse symbols, revoice, silently quantize, export stale state, or depend on a CDN. SMF headers, chunks, VLQs, running status, track counts, and byte order are deterministic.

Independent minimal SMF parser and golden hashes; headers/chunks/VLQ/running-status, 2/2 through 6/8, BPM bounds, Manual/Frozen, external bass, loss report, stale/missing realization, filenames and object-URL cleanup. Log stable identities, inputs, limits, termination and exact diffs without leaking chart content unnecessarily.

## Non-goals
No MIDI import, live device access, General MIDI sound claim, microtonal pitch bends, or UI. Preserve unrelated work.

## Background

## Required implementation
Compile typed melody, bass, chord, rhythm, range, style and endpoint constraints into legal candidates via T1/G0/G2/V2. Separate hard constraints from soft cost axes; return Pareto solutions or actionable conflict sets, stats, termination and exact revision-checked patch.

Never invent coverage for an impossible note, silently reinterpret spelling, relax pins, merge hard/soft requirements, mutate during search, or confuse literal identity with contextual reading.

Small spaces equal brute-force enumeration; every solution satisfies every hard constraint; unsatisfiable cases identify the actual conflicting slots/rules; cancellation/resume/yield order is deterministic.

## Test plan and detailed logging
Independent brute-force oracle; melody/bass/spelling near misses, contradictory pins, exact rhythm, Manual/Frozen, plural/no context, 16/128/100k bounds, memory counters, transposition, ties, cancellation, stale patch and performance observation. Log stable identities, inputs, limits, termination and exact diffs without leaking chart content unnecessarily.

## Non-goals
No audio transcription, melody extraction, probabilistic inference, or UI. Preserve unrelated work.

title: G7: Cadence, phrase, harmonic-rhythm, and tension-curve transforms
description:
## Background
This is reviewed plan package G7 in the Advanced Craft milestone and implements selected deterministic Idea Wizard capabilities.

## Required implementation
Detect phrase/cadence opportunities from G0/H1 with strict positive/near-miss rules. Emit exact TransformLaw patches for supported approaches, turnarounds, backdoor/secondary/diminished setups, anticipation, delay, split/merge, augmentation/diminution and metric displacement. Compute a deterministic tension curve from named axes: function, dissonance, voice motion, register, harmonic rhythm and context confidence.

## Invariants and risks
Preserve exact BeatValue and measure accounting unless the explicit bounded request changes them. Do not label cadence from roots alone, insert hidden rests, apply near-miss rules or portray tension as musical quality.

## Success criteria
Every candidate names phrase evidence, law, exact before/after timing, axis deltas, limitations and conflicts; transforms undo cleanly, remain PPQ-integral and visibly refuse unsupported contexts.

## Test plan and detailed logging
Cadence positives/near misses; exact-time properties across meters for every rhythm transform; component/mutation/transposition tests for curves; pickup/incomplete measures, Manual/Frozen boundaries, stale/nonmutating patches, deterministic ranks and caps. Log identities, evidence, limits, termination and exact diffs.

## Non-goals
No beat tracking from audio, genre-authenticity claim, or UI. Preserve unrelated work.

title: G8: Motif, sequence, and nonfunctional transformation atlas
description:
## Background
This is reviewed plan package G8 in the Advanced Craft milestone and implements selected deterministic Idea Wizard capabilities.

## Required implementation
Extract typed motifs and generate bounded diatonic, chromatic and intervallic sequences with exact target landings, spelling policy, rhythm preservation and proof chain. Add explicitly limited common-tone, planing, chromatic-mediant and neo-Riemannian P/L/R laws on eligible triads with preserved tones, exact voice motion and refusal outside domain.

## Invariants and risks
Do not infer motifs from arbitrary repetition, apply P/L/R to seventh/custom/unsupported sonorities, overclaim functional explanation, lose enharmonic rationale or ignore landing/range/measure constraints. Every variant passes normal parser/resolver/validation laws.

## Success criteria
Transforms land exactly or refuse, preserve declared rhythm/common tones, state relation/domain/limitations, dedupe by stable identity and obey declared transpose/inverse laws.

## Test plan and detailed logging
Motif false positives; diatonic/chromatic sequences and landing failures; meters/ranges; P/L/R truth tables and ineligible near misses; common-tone/planing/mediant goldens, spelling alternatives, inverse/metamorphic/transposition, deterministic bounds and mutation tests. Log identities, evidence, limits, termination and exact diffs.

## Non-goals
No Schenkerian-analysis claim, arbitrary graph embedding, style imitation, or UI. Preserve unrelated work.

title: G9: Deterministic Chart-to-Practice Laboratory engine
description:
## Background
This is reviewed plan package G9 in the Advanced Craft milestone and implements selected deterministic Idea Wizard capabilities.

## Required implementation
Define versioned PracticeTemplate, Session, Prompt, Answer and Rubric records. Generate bounded seeded chart-derived exercises for spelling, chord roles, guide tones, voice leading, context, cadence/law recognition, constrained completion, reharmonization comparison and finite playback/listening questions. Record seed/engine/content/source versions and grade exact allowed answers with itemized arithmetic rubrics.

## Invariants and risks
Never grade subjective taste as correct, generate runtime content with a model, self-certify answer corpora, or let chart edits silently change an active session. Keep suggested versus required explicit.

## Success criteria
Same seed/template/source produces identical prompts/order/answers; every objective item has independently reviewed accepted answers and near misses; partial credit and ambiguous alternatives are transparent; stale sessions freeze or restart explicitly.

## Test plan and detailed logging
Golden session per template, seed reproducibility/distribution, finite-answer completeness, mutation/near-miss grading, enharmonic policy, ambiguous context, no-subjective-grade audit, empty/unsupported charts, stale revisions, bounds, audio metadata and serialization. Log identities, evidence, limits, termination and exact diffs.

## Non-goals
No user model, cloud account, spaced-repetition scheduler, generative tutor, or UI. Preserve unrelated work.

## Background

Implement deterministic order-preserving sequence-alignment DP for 3-7 voices with explicit entering/leaving gaps, stable request-local voice IDs/ordinals, degree provenance, exact/pitch-class/spelled identity distinctions, and VoiceArc endpoints. Propagate IDs on matches, allocate entering IDs, forbid crossing by construction, and return plural motion costs without string-prefix matching.

Entering/leaving semitones are null, not zero. Octave common tone, exact sustained identity, and spelled identity are distinct questions. ## Non-goals

## Package contract carried into this task
### G0: Implement phrase analysis and k-best Tonal Journey paths

## Background
This is reviewed plan package G0 in Musical Intelligence. It expands the trusted editor with deterministic, evidence-bearing theory rather than opaque recommendation.

## Required implementation
Build pure deterministic phrase/cadence feature extraction and bounded k-best sequence analysis over major/minor/mode tonic contexts plus tonicization, modal/nonfunctional, no-key, and unclassified states. Score with typed evidence/counterevidence from literal match, duration/metric emphasis, neighbor resolution, cadence, and section assertions. Return five non-dominated paths with key-area spans, pivots, modulation boundaries, phrase/cadence roles, missing evidence, and user-pinnable reading IDs.

## Invariants and risks
This is plural analysis, not key detection truth. It cannot silently persist context, force planing into functional labels, use wall time semantically, or collapse ambiguous paths. Use resumable deterministic work quanta for long charts.

## Success criteria
Same chart/versions yields identical paths/order/stats; pinned/no-key ranges respected; positive/near-miss cadences and pivots classified honestly; 256 events meet performance gate without blocking UI runner.

## Test plan and detailed logging
tests/conformance/tonal-journey.test.ts and tonal-ambiguity tests across modulations, tonicizations, modal vamps, planing, ordinary/secondary dominants, pivot alternatives, missing key, section overrides, transposition, caps/degraded/stale/cancel, and five-path determinism.

## Non-goals
No runtime AI, network, universal musical-quality score, hidden constraint relaxation, or implementation-generated authority. Do not oversimplify away ambiguity, proof, limits, or alternatives. Preserve unrelated work.

## This subtask
Materialize the code-facing contract before the production implementation: module ownership and dependency boundaries; public types and result/refusal/diagnostic shapes; stable identities and version fields; every numeric/collection/work/memory limit; deterministic ordering and tie-breaks; state transitions where relevant; and an independently authored fixture or state matrix for the positive, near-miss, malformed, limit, cancellation, and stale cases named above.

## Deliverables
- Checked-in interfaces/types, fixture records, goldens or UI/audio state matrices appropriate to this package.
- A compact authority/provenance ledger for judgment-bearing musical or content expectations.
- Exact trace links from each parent invariant and success criterion to a fixture/test identifier.
- A handoff note in code or test documentation explaining assumptions and forbidden shortcuts.

## Exit criteria
Artifacts typecheck/validate without intentionally failing or skipped gates. Expected results are not generated by the production algorithm they will test. Another agent can implement the package from this bead and its checked-in artifacts without consulting the markdown plan. No production shortcut or feature reduction is authorized.
notes: MTDT chord-mining refinement (2026-07-22): phrase and cadence evidence uses an explicit status lattice candidate -> supported -> attenuated -> closed. A chord pair alone never certifies closure. Meter, duration, phrase boundary, soprano and bass arrival, cadential-six-four evidence, deceptive variants, tonicized half cadence, restart evidence, pedals, and reopened continuation contribute separately with positive and near-miss fixtures. Expose structural progression spans and sequence membership so surface stations are not each misclassified as independent functional decisions.

title: G2: Implement the explainable Contextual Continuation Engine
description:
## Background
This is reviewed plan package G2 in Musical Intelligence. It expands the trusted editor with deterministic, evidence-bearing theory rather than opaque recommendation.

## Required implementation
Implement provider registry over prior 1-4 events, Tonal Journey/phrase context, injected AtlasQuery fixture, root/bass/guide motion, repetition, cadence, and color. Providers generate exact timed edit plans for functional, modal, chromatic, diminished, sequence, pedal/line-cliche, and nonfunctional continuations. Canonical-dedupe, hard-filter, Pareto-prune, and category/rank with visible Smooth/Functional/Colorful/Exploratory policies. Emit HarmonicProof, source revision, why/why-not, <=32/provider and <=16 display options via resumable stepper.

## Invariants and risks
Full Atlas enrichment arrives in D0; core must work law-only. Wall time cannot change results. Candidate IDs/order must be byte-deterministic; hard constraints/timing/stale source never relax/apply. No corpus occurrence is treated as correctness.

## Success criteria
Every displayed candidate revalidates and is source/timing/proof complete; categories provide meaningfully distinct options; no-result/degraded/cancelled/stale envelopes complete; eight-event search meets 100ms performance gate.

## Test plan and detailed logging
tests/conformance/continuation.test.ts and continuation-limits tests for every provider/near miss, context windows, policy ordering, Pareto/dedup, stable IDs, exact edits, stale revision, cap/degraded/no-result/cancel, all-root transposition, fixture corpus enrichment, and mutation of laws/evidence.

## Non-goals
No runtime AI, network, universal musical-quality score, hidden constraint relaxation, or implementation-generated authority. Do not oversimplify away ambiguity, proof, limits, or alternatives. Preserve unrelated work.

title: U3: Build the evidence-first Harmony Lens and motion explanations
description:
## Background
This is reviewed plan package U3 in Musical Intelligence. It expands the trusted editor with deterministic, evidence-bearing theory rather than opaque recommendation.

## Required implementation
Extend inspector with Literal facts first, then plural Context readings, chord-scale/tension candidates, evidence tiers/counter/missing evidence, law-valid options, and pairwise voice motion. Render canonical degrees/spellings/guide tones/bass/alt realizations, Roman/quality/context classification, scale containment/clashes, and source rule/citation disclosure. Provide Preview/Apply only through application intents and clearly separate facts/readings/options.

## Invariants and risks
No uncalibrated confidence, “the scale,” universal resolution judgment, hidden persistence, or color-only evidence. Empty/no-key/ambiguous/unclassified/custom/unsupported states require honest copy. UI cannot call theory/audio directly.

## Success criteria
Keyboard/touch/screen-reader users can inspect all layers and understand why/why-not without mutation; stale options disable; motion arcs/equality identities accurate; responsive tab/disclosure states pass.

## Test plan and detailed logging
E2E for literal/context/scale/motion/custom/alt/no-key/ambiguous/stale/no-result, every evidence tier, rule disclosure, Preview/Apply/Undo, keyboard/focus/live regions, mobile sheets, 200%/forced-color snapshots, and motion/regression assertions.

## Non-goals
No runtime AI, network, universal musical-quality score, hidden constraint relaxation, or implementation-generated authority. Do not oversimplify away ambiguity, proof, limits, or alternatives. Preserve unrelated work.

title: Epic: Reliable Studio — author, recover, import, play, and stop
description:
## Background
This milestone turns the trustworthy core into a real progression editor and eliminates the legacy data-loss, touch, transport, preview, and stale-audio failures.

## Goals
- Command/history state with stable-ID selection and transactional replacement.
- Recovery, canonical/legacy import/export, lead-sheet chart editing, inspector, piano.
- Exact local voicing and playback plans.
- One lazy persistent Web Audio graph with serialized transport and strict no-future-attack Stop.
- Responsive accessible shell, real preview, transport, and lifecycle dialogs.

## Included plan packages
A0, A1, C0, P0, V0, X0, X1, E0, U0, U1, U2, U4, U5.

## Guardrails
No UI calls audio/storage directly; no import applies before confirmation; manual/custom pitches remain exact; preview is nonmutating; document replacement retires all audio generations before publish; all UI/audio integration waits on X1 stop-safety.

## Epic exit
A user can create/edit/reorder/undo/recover/migrate/import/export JSON or chart text and reliably preview/play/pause/seek/stop/replay on keyboard, pointer, and touch, with failure E2E and no stale audio.

title: A0: Implement application commands, history, bookmarks, and selectors
description:
## Background
This is reviewed plan package A0 in the Reliable Studio milestone. It must eliminate a documented legacy failure class while preserving the Foundation contracts.

## Test plan and detailed logging
Integration/property tests for every command/inverse, coalescing boundaries, eviction, import undo/redo, ID collisions, selection/focus after deletion/reorder, stale request IDs, old transport notifications, and 1,000 randomized edit/undo sequences with seed/action log.

## Non-goals
Do not substitute mocks where this package names real adapters/audio/browser behavior, and do not weaken exact musical/data semantics to make UI integration easier. Preserve unrelated work.

## U1-CMP-007 InsertionPlanNotice
previewInsertionPlan() states exactly one of the five statements for the current draft and target, and dispatches nothing. It reuses completeDraftPlacement — the same chooser applyQuickEntryPreview uses — so the statement cannot drift from the dispatch. The notice renders in the quick-entry panel with its explicit resolutions, and canInsert is now driven by plan.committable, so the statement and the affordance can never disagree.

### One thing the classification got wrong first, and why
The first version returned not-atomic-refusal for a short bar, because it checked draft.status !== 'ready' before looking at anything else. In fact T0 REFUSES an underfilled bar outright with chart.bar_underfilled rather than publishing a short measure, so 'the draft leaves a short bar' is visible only in the diagnostics. A draft refused for nothing but chart.bar_underfilled is now the incomplete case; anything else is a genuine non-atomic refusal. The draft's own status is no longer consulted at all — it is a summary, and the two blocked statements need the diagnostic to be told apart. A short-bar check I had written over the parsed draft was dead code and is gone: the parser returns no draft at all in that case.

### A work-bound fix
previewInsertionPlan re-parses the draft, and calling it during render would have re-parsed on every render. U1_WORK_BOUNDS.previewTokenVisits is 'at-most-maxPreviewTokens-per-draft-change', so it is now behind a useMemo keyed on the draft text, its target, and the revision.

## A targeting inconsistency, fixed
The measure target button set bookmarks.insertion, but the quick-entry draft carries its OWN target (state.quickEntry.target), and quickEntryTarget() re-derived from the insertion bookmark on every keystroke. Aiming at a measure after typing therefore left the plan and the eventual dispatch pointed at the previous measure. Now: a draft keeps the target it was aimed at, the bookmark is only the fallback for a draft with no target, the measure button re-aims the existing draft through exactly one set-quick-entry intent (U1-OP-002), and the highlighted target reads from quickEntry.targetId. The view model gained brand-free quickEntry.target/targetId for this, mirroring rangeAnchor/rangeFocus.

## U1-OP-005 recovered-chord lane (the largest remaining gap, now closed)
`insertRecoveredChord(globalOrdinal, callerBeatText, acknowledgement, incompleteReason)` builds the A0 `RecoveredChordInsertFragmentEditPlan` and dispatches exactly one `apply-edit-plan` command. `previewQuickEntryDraft()` replaced the planned separate preview: one bounded T0 parse now answers both the token rows and the lane state, so the declared at-most-maxPreviewTokens-per-draft-change work bound still holds with the App memoising it on (draft text, target id, revision).

Token rows implement U1-CMP-004/005, which did not exist at all: a parsed draft yields one `valid` row per parsed event; a refused draft yields one `insertable` row per chord T0 published plus one `invalid` row per diagnostic and no `valid` rows, exactly as contract 4 requires. Every row's `sourceText` is the exact draft slice taken from T0's own source range; nothing is repaired, canonicalised, or guessed.

### The acknowledgement is a real gesture, not a formality
The A0 plan type pins `layoutLossAcknowledgement` to the literal, so a typed caller cannot construct a wrong one and `edit-plan.recovered-chord-layout-loss-unacknowledged` is unreachable from U1. Rather than fabricate that A0 refusal, the surface carries the literal from a checkbox the caller ticks into the controller call, and the controller refuses `u1.quick_entry_lane_mismatch` when what arrives is not the literal — 4.2 states the acknowledgement as a precondition *of the lane*, so a request without it is not a recovered-chord request. The closed U1 refusal inventory is unchanged; no new code was invented.

### Capacity and duration are exact, and a short bar stays explicit
A resolved T0 duration must fit the destination remainder; a `requires-caller` duration needs a positive remainder plus exact caller beat text. Supplying a duration for a chord T0 already resolved refuses `u1.duration_invalid` rather than being ignored. After the insert the destination's completion is recomputed exactly by the same `completionAfterEdit` the other edits use: exact fill publishes `complete`, a short bar refuses `u1.completion_reason_required` and routes through the measure-completion dialog, and an overfill refuses `u1.duration_overfills_measure`. No rest is synthesised and no bar is rebalanced.

## Contract 5.3 dirty-draft prompt
Switching away from an inline symbol editor holding a draft that differs from the chord's stored text now records the interrupted transition verbatim (`DeferredSwitch`) and prompts Apply, Discard, or Continue editing. Apply commits and then performs the interrupted action; Discard closes the editor, restoring the exact stored text, and then performs it; Continue editing dismisses the prompt and refocuses the field. Blur stays completely inert, and a draft typed back to its stored text is not dirty, so it never prompts.

## The three component shapes the inventory declares
- U1-CMP-019 MeasureCompletionDialog is now a real modal `Dialog` in `#dialog-host` with the reason field, Confirm disabled until a reason exists, and Cancel. It opens when an operation is interrupted by a reason-required refusal, and from the `Declare this measure's completion` card-menu item; nothing is declared until Confirm, so a short bar is never declared in passing.
- U1-CMP-020 SectionBoundaryMenu is now a menu with two `menuitemradio` items naming both boundaries plus Join with next section, replacing a toggle button whose next state the caller had to infer.
- U1-CMP-023 RangeBoundaryHandle now exists: two threshold-gated draggable handles that set their own edge from the card they are dropped on. Drag stays optional — each handle's own activation, Set start/Set end, and the exact beat fields all reach the same edge without a pointer.

## Nine declared key bindings were missing or wrong
`U1_KEY_BINDINGS` is a closed table; the implementation honoured 29 of its 38 rows. Fixed: Alt+M was bound to move-following (U1-OP-013, whose declared access is a menu item) instead of move-to-boundary (U1-OP-012); Alt+K, Alt+L, Alt+C and Alt+B (split-section, join-sections, set-measure-completion, set-section-boundary) did nothing at all; the range scope had no Home, End or Escape. Structural chart shortcuts act on the measure the insertion point names, then the focused card's measure, then the first measure — the insertion point wins because it is the published bookmark for where structural work goes.

`declareMeasureCompletion(measureId, reason)` was added for Alt+C: it publishes the completion the measure's own exact fill implies. On a measure whose stored completion already matches, A0 refuses `command.payload_invalid` and U1 surfaces that verbatim rather than rewriting it into a U1 code.

## Three defects found and fixed while proving this
1. A completed handle drag ends with a click on the captured handle, so the drop and the handle's own activation both published an edge — two boundaries from one gesture. The click that closes a real drag is now consumed.
2. The range bar rendered `Range ? to ? beats` whenever the two edges were the same boundary, because `selectBeatRange` correctly returns null for a span of no beats. It now says so instead of printing question marks; it still never invents a beat label.
3. The measure-completion dialog first opened from a button inside the refusal notice. The U0 `Dialog` restores focus to its declared trigger, and a successful Confirm removes the refusal — so every successful declaration raised `ui.stale_owner` and dropped focus to the workspace fallback. The dialog now names the chart region as its owner, which outlives every notice, and it opens by itself when an operation is interrupted by a reason-required refusal. U1-OP-019's declared pointer alternative is a `Declare this measure's completion` card-menu item; a chart-toolbar button was tried first and rejected, because the extra toolbar row pushed the append-measure control's centre below the 390 px coarse viewport and broke the U0 target-ownership gate.

## Still remaining on this leaf
1. WebKit cannot launch on this host (needs `sudo apt-get install libgtk-4-1 libicu74 libavif16 libmanette-0.2-0 libenchant-2-2 libhyphen0 libwoff1`). Unchanged from checkpoint 10.
2. `u1-editing-contract.ts` still reports `specified-not-implemented`, byte-pinned by `tests/static/u1-contract.test.ts`; flipping it belongs to the verify leaf .10.3.

## Exact commands and results (checkpoint 11, all local, all after the final edit)
- `/home/ubuntu/.bun/bin/bun --bun test` -> 2289 pass, 0 fail across 218 files, 481,459 assertions (721.97 s). The plain `bun test` form is still intercepted by the RCH remote offload and dies; the `--bun` form stays local.
- `bun scripts/run-playwright.ts test --project=chromium` -> 118 passed (2.0 m).
- `bun scripts/run-playwright.ts test --project=firefox` -> 118 passed (3.2 m).
- `bun run verify:reproducible` -> pass, sha256 9ee34bfc4cd7146d826457b8ce0fc6fb6da65df3f15d82c2104c7b5f63856e19, 794,042 bytes, rebuilt in isolated roots with differing mtimes.
- `bun run verify:standalone` -> static inspection outcome pass; 24 cells passed, 12 failed, every failure `[webkit]` and zero Chromium or Firefox failures. Unchanged from checkpoint 10: WebKit still cannot launch on this host.
- `bun run validate:u1-contract` -> outcome pass, findings []. `bun run validate:a0-u1-edit-plan-contract` -> outcome pass.
- `bun run typecheck` clean; `bun run lint` outcome pass, 0 findings across 142 files.
- Artifact 794,042 bytes against the unchanged 1,048,576 shell ceiling: 254,534 bytes of headroom, and the 524,288-byte Atlas reservation untouched.

New evidence added by this checkpoint: 11 recovered-lane cases in `tests/integration/u1-edit-channel.test.ts`, 4 quick-entry E2E cases, 4 inline-edit E2E cases for the dirty-draft prompt, 3 range E2E cases for the boundary handles and the range-scope keys, and 2 pointer/keyboard E2E cases for the repaired shortcut table.

All 33 operations and all 38 declared bindings resolve to exactly one application command or intent; no U1 refusal code was invented and no A0 refusal is rewritten. Three defects were found and fixed while proving it: a completed handle drag published two boundaries from one gesture, the range bar printed question marks for a span of no beats, and the completion dialog raised ui.stale_owner on every successful confirm. title: U1/verify: Prove conformance, integration, and evidence
description:
## Package contract carried into this task
### U1: Build quick entry and stable-ID lead-sheet chart editing

## Background
This is reviewed plan package U1 in the Reliable Studio milestone. It must eliminate a documented legacy failure class while preserving the Foundation contracts.

## Required implementation
Implement QuickEntry raw draft/parsed preview/token errors, whole-chart atomic apply and explicit one-token insertion; semantic chart with sections/measures/chord cards/insertion targets; select/shift range/touch Set Start-End; inline valid-on-Apply symbol edit; insert/duplicate/delete/move/split/join/duration/section operations; optional pointer drag plus complete keyboard/menu alternatives; stable roving focus; measure fit/split/rebalance/incomplete confirmation; compact/teaching views.

## Invariants and risks
Touch preventDefault only after real drag threshold; component listeners/pointer capture clean up once. Selection/insertion/range/playhead remain distinct. Blur never coerces invalid text. No index keys, beat loss, hidden rests, silent rebalance, or drag-required authoring.

## Success criteria
Desktop/mobile/keyboard/touch users can author/reorder/range/edit charts with correct focus/IDs/history/measure timing; parse errors and all empty/overfill states are clear; listener counts stay constant.

## Test plan and detailed logging
E2E quick entry/chart/touch/reorder/focus/range/measure workflows at named viewports, property tests for stable-ID commands, repeated mount/reorder listener counts, pointer cancel/unmount, text errors, Delete+Undo, and L-TOUCH/L-STATE regressions with action/focus logs.

## Non-goals
Do not substitute mocks where this package names real adapters/audio/browser behavior, and do not weaken exact musical/data semantics to make UI integration easier. Preserve unrelated work.

## This subtask
Independently verify the implemented package against every named success criterion and test case above. Complete the package-specific unit/property/metamorphic/golden/mutation/integration/browser/audio/accessibility/performance evidence that applies; use real adapters whenever the contract names them. Exercise positive, near-miss, refusal, limit, cancellation, resume, stale revision, cleanup, and deterministic replay paths with detailed reproducible logs.

## Deliverables
- The complete named test suite and machine-readable logs/snapshots/hashes/counters.
- A trace ledger showing every parent requirement, invariant, success criterion, and legacy/Idea-Wizard regression has evidence.
- Reviewed baselines and explicit limitations only where the parent contract permits them.
- Targeted fixes plus regression tests for defects found during verification.

## Exit criteria
All package gates are green from a clean invocation, no unexplained retry/skip/quarantine exists, no serious console/leak/nondeterminism issue remains, and the evidence is sufficient to close the parent package. Record commands, versions, seeds, environment and concise results in the bead closeout.
notes:
PROGRESS CHECKPOINT 2 (2026-07-26, agent SwiftStone). The leaf's four remaining bodies of work are done: every operation-matrix row is driven, the interaction matrix is driven except four cases blocked on packages U1 does not own, all 18 laws now carry executed evidence on both polarities, and the three-browser matrix runs for the first time.

## The WebKit blocker is gone

WebKit could not launch on this host. Playwright's own dependency check named `libicu74`, but that was only the part it could map to a package: the shipped `minibrowser-gtk/bin/MiniBrowser` and `minibrowser-wpe/bin/MiniBrowser` also needed `libjxl.so.0.8` and `libbacktrace.so.0`, none of which exist in Ubuntu 25.10 (questing ships ICU 76 and libjxl 0.11).

Resolved without weakening anything: `libbacktrace0` from the distro, `libicu74` extracted from the Ubuntu noble `.deb`, and `libjxl0.8` (0.8.2-4) from `snapshot.debian.org` with its published SHA-1 verified (`c1c988354228bd71045461af25b6442d1d758484`). The four ICU sonames and the two libjxl sonames were copied into the two `webkit-2311` bundle `lib/` directories, which is where Playwright already points `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. `ldd` now reports nothing missing for either MiniBrowser.

- The very first WebKit run passed 126 of 126 with no WebKit-specific defect behind the launch failure. Two defects did surface later, once the new specs exercised focus — see below; both were latent in every engine and only WebKit made them observable.

Extraction root, for reproduction: `~/.cache/ms-playwright-extra-deps/`.

## Every non-positive operation-matrix row is now driven

`tests/integration/u1-refusal-rows.test.ts` (new, 14 tests) closes the eleven rows that `u1-edit-channel.test.ts` could not reach. All 59 rows — 36 positive plus 23 non-positive — are now driven or have their unreachability measured.

`tests/support/u1-chart-fixture.ts` (new) is what makes that possible. Quick entry can only ever produce Auto voicings and can only grow a chart one publication at a time, so two families of rows were out of reach through the product's own entry path. The fixture authors a candidate document and publishes it through the same real F2 decode and F3 semantic boundary the product uses; a candidate either boundary refuses is reported as a refusal rather than forced in. A chart that already carries stored pitches is what a user reopens, so this is an ordinary document fact rather than the U2 operation the previous checkpoint assumed it needed.

- **U1-OPC-036 / U1-OPC-037** (Manual and Frozen voicing block the inline rename) now run against a real chord with real stored pitches. Both refuse `u1.symbol_edit_blocked_manual_voicing` with the revision unmoved, and a third test proves the rendered chart is byte-identical after each refusal.
- **U1-OPC-050** (a selection of exactly 8,192 chords) runs against a chart at the exact document capacity: 1,024 measures of eight eighth-notes. The extend is one `ephemeral-updated` intent, the selection holds exactly 8,192 ids, and the revision does not move.
- **U1-OPC-051** (8,193 chords refuse with `u1.selection_limit`) is **unreachable, and now provably so**: `MAX_SELECTED_EVENT_IDS` is not an independent number, it *is* `MAX_DOCUMENT_CHORD_EVENTS`. The test asserts that equality and then shows that a document holding one more event is refused by F2. The guard's refusal branch has no valid document to live in.
- **U1-OPC-052** (a T0-refused draft dispatched so A0 can answer `edit-plan.syntax-refused`) is likewise unreachable, for the opposite reason: the surface *can* see the refusal in advance. `previewInsertionPlan()` states `not-atomic-refusal` and `applyQuickEntryPreview()` refuses `u1.insertion_plan_not_atomic` before dispatch, with no command published and the draft text untouched. That is strictly stronger than the row asks for — the same shape as the U1-QE-043/044 finding in checkpoint 1.
- **U1-OPC-054** (two Duplicate activations in one frame) drives two activations with no clock tick between them: each advances the revision by exactly one and each is its own undo step. Neither batched nor nested.
- **U1-OPC-035** (`command.wrong_document`) cannot arise from this surface: `replace-document` is frozen outside the U1 command surface, so the test drives insert, duplicate, rename, insert-section, undo and redo and proves the document identity never moves. The mismatch the row needs has no U1 gesture that can create it.
- **U1-OPC-034** (a stale Delete) holds one step earlier: the Delete gesture captures no revision at all, it reads the live snapshot at dispatch. The test advances the revision out of band and shows the following Delete is the correct command against current state.
- **U1-OPC-053** (`u1.operation_not_authorized`) is proved behaviourally rather than by inspection. The six unauthorized kinds each move a value U1 must never move, so the test drives the surface hard against a chart with a Manual voicing and asserts that meter, key, tempo, instrument, volumes, count-in, document identity, the stored chord's symbol and its voicing mode are all exactly where they started.
- **U1-OPC-056 / U1-OPC-057** (pointer capture lost, and a release below the threshold) are driven in the browser — see below.

## The interaction-state matrix: 54 of 58, with the other four explained

`tests/integration/u1-interaction-states.test.ts` (new, 10 tests) covers the states whose subject is application state: U1-INT-005 (selecting never moves the insertion point, and the three bookmarks hold three different values at once while the playhead does not move), U1-INT-014 and U1-INT-015 (the declared delete-repair order, falling back to the previous event and then to the section insertion target, never to the document body), U1-INT-050 (clearing the draft is one ephemeral intent), U1-INT-051, U1-INT-052 (an out-of-band undo repairs the bookmark and publishes a focus request), and U1-INT-046/047.

`tests/e2e/u1-pointer-listeners.spec.ts` (new, 10 tests) and `tests/e2e/u1-empty-errors.spec.ts` (new, 7 tests) cover the states whose subject is the rendered surface, all against the real generated artifact: the 8 CSS-pixel threshold and the `preventDefault` that waits for it (U1-INT-017/018, U1-OPC-057), pointer cancel and mid-drag unmount (U1-OPC-056, U1-INT-020), the three transient listeners and their release (U1-INT-025), per-card listener totals across ten reorders of twenty cards (U1-INT-023), a whole authoring session on the keyboard alone (U1-INT-021), the empty chart and empty selection (U1-INT-042/045), individually visible token errors (U1-INT-043), exact beats and stored reasons (U1-INT-046/047), and clean cancellation of an inline edit and of the completion dialog (U1-INT-048/049).

The four that are **not** driven, and why:

1. **U1-INT-002** ("playback advances across three chords") and **U1-INT-003** ("a chord preview is auditioned from the card menu") need playback and audition. The studio transport reports `status: "unavailable"`, `isAvailable: false` — X0/X1 are not wired to it yet. These are blocked on those packages, not on U1.
2. **U1-INT-006** states its precondition as "playhead at beat 12". No U1 operation can move the playhead — that is exactly the law it tests — and nothing else can either until the transport is wired. Its three-bookmark half is asserted in `U1-INT-005`; its rendered-accessible-name half is not, so the case is deliberately left unlinked rather than half-claimed.
3. **U1-INT-026** ("the chart region is unmounted") has no product path: `StudioShell` mounts `ChartWorkspace` unconditionally for the lifetime of the app. The leak class it guards is covered instead by U1-INT-020 (a card unmounted mid-drag) and U1-INT-023 (per-card totals across ten reorders).

## Law coverage is complete on both polarities

The emitted ledger at `test-results/u1-evidence/trace-ledger.json` now reports **18 of 18 laws with executed evidence on both polarities**, up from 17 at the last checkpoint and 10 when the ledger was first computed. Named case ids rose from 70 to 100. Every per-law floor in `PINNED_FLOOR` was raised to the measured value, and `lawsWithBothPolarities` is now pinned at 18: coverage may rise, never fall.

Four laws still have a declared case with no executed evidence, and all four are the cases listed above: U1-EDIT-003 (19/20 negative), U1-EDIT-008 (10/13 positive), U1-EDIT-015 (3/4 positive), U1-EDIT-017 (7/8 negative).

## The browser proofs read the reviewed numbers instead of copying them

`u1-pointer-listeners.spec.ts` reads `pointerPolicy.dragThresholdCssPx`, `listenerPolicy.transientDragListenersPerSession` and `listenerPolicy.maxConcurrentDragSessions` out of the fixture packet rather than restating them as literals. That is what makes the browser proof mutation-sensitive: `U1-MUT-021` changes the threshold and `U1-MUT-024` changes the listener budget, and a private copy of those numbers here would let the production surface keep passing against a packet that no longer says what it says. The validator's own replay of all 32 controls stays green (`mutationControlsReplayed: 32`).

## Six defects found and fixed

1. **Renaming the chart after any chord edit was refused.** `setTitle` stamped its command from a private clock, `(ordinal - 1) * TITLE_COMMAND_INTERVAL_MS`, that started at zero and never saw the shared logical clock every other command advances. The first rename after any edit therefore travelled backwards in logical time and A0 refused it with `command.logical_time_invalid`. Every real session hits this — the user types changes, then names the chart. The spacing that keeps consecutive renames out of the text-coalescing window is now measured *from* the shared clock instead of replacing it, so renames are still separate undo entries with exact snapshots. Three regression tests: rename after an edit, two renames staying separate undo steps, and a rename interleaved between two edits.
2. **A card unmounted mid-drag wedged dragging permanently.** `useEffect(() => endDragSession, [])` released the session only when the whole chart region unmounted. When an undo or a delete repair removed the card a drag was holding, the detached handle could never fire `pointerup` or `pointercancel` again, so `dragSession.current` stayed set and `beginDrag` returned early on every later attempt — dragging was dead for the rest of the session. Found by driving U1-INT-020, whose "and the surface is not wedged: a fresh drag still starts" assertion failed. Now released per card when its handle leaves the document, which is the "capture is released on unmount" half of the reviewed pointer policy.
3. **An overfilling duration notice stated no numbers.** U1-INT-046 requires the exact current fill, the exact resulting fill and the capacity as rationals; the message said only "The new duration changes the measure fill and needs an explicit decision." `completionAfterEdit` now returns the exact resulting total and the capacity with its refusal, and the duration path states all three ("This measure holds 4/1 of 4/1 beats; the new duration would make it 7/1.").
4. **A short measure never showed its stored reason.** U1-INT-047 requires the declared reason to be displayed with the measure and never invented. The reason was stored in the document and dropped at the view-model boundary. `StudioMeasureViewModel` now carries `completionReason` — verbatim for `incomplete` and `pickup`, `null` otherwise — and the chart renders it as a measure fact in both views, because a stored reason is a musical fact the author supplied rather than an analysis the teaching view adds.
5. **T0 diagnostic ranges were not surfaced.** §6 requires T0 codes *and ranges* verbatim; the token row showed only the code. `StudioQuickEntryToken` now carries `diagnosticRange` and the row renders it, so a reader can find the offending characters in a long draft.
6. **The inline editors were unreachable from the keyboard, and cancelling one stranded the caret.** `autoFocus` on a dynamically inserted input is not portable. Chromium and Firefox ignored it, so F2 opened an editor the caret never entered — every keystroke went to the card underneath and the "type, then Enter" path the contract describes never worked. WebKit honoured it and then dropped focus to the **document body** when the input unmounted, so every key after a cancelled edit reached nothing at all. The same gap existed after any command: the A0 focus-request renderer was a passive `useEffect`, which runs after the browser is already free to deliver the next key, so on WebKit focus sat on the body between a move and its repair. Focus is now moved explicitly when an editor opens and returned to the owning card when it closes, and both the editor effect and the A0 focus-request renderer are `useLayoutEffect`s so the repair lands before the next event can be dispatched. Two regression tests assert both halves, and they pass identically in all three engines.

Also fixed: one order-dependent E2E. `U1-INT-021` pressed Enter into a draft the surface had not yet classified, which passed in isolation and failed once in the full Chromium run. It now waits for the Insert control to become enabled — the same signal a user waits for — before publishing, and polls for the reorder instead of asserting it instantly. It then failed once more under full-project load on a different assertion, so the whole chain was hardened: every keystroke now waits for an observable settle — focus, selection count, or dialog state — before the next one is sent, because a key delivered into a half-applied state is dropped and a dropped key is a flake rather than a finding.

## The implementation-status flip, and the part of it that is not this leaf's to make

`U1_EDITING_IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS` in `src/ui/studio/u1-editing-contract.ts` is now `"implemented-live"`, with the reasoning recorded at the constant.

The fixture packet's four claim flags stay false, and that is deliberate rather than unfinished. `scripts/validate-u1-contract.ts` hard-requires `productionImplementationClaim`, `uiCompletionClaim`, `humanAcceptanceClaim` and `expertReviewClaim` to be exactly `false`, and `tests/static/u1-contract.test.ts` proves the validator rejects a packet that sets them. Those flags are the *specification* leaf's statement about itself — they exist so the packet can never be read as evidence for the code it was written to judge. Flipping them means editing the independent oracle, which the sibling A0/U1 packet only did under a recorded human acceptance ("Accept A0/U1 reconciliation packet R1", 2026-07-24). No such acceptance exists for U1, so the flags were left alone and this is filed as the decision the user owns.

## Two observations recorded, not papered over

- `U1_REFUSAL_CODES` declares 29 codes; production implements 24. The five with no production site are `u1.preview_token_limit`, `u1.duration_underfills_measure_requires_reason` (production uses the declared `u1.completion_reason_required` for that state), `u1.stale_revision` (production uses the more precise `u1.quick_entry_stale_revision`, and no other gesture captures a revision to go stale), `u1.pointer_capture_lost` and `u1.operation_not_authorized` (both describe states the surface reaches without needing to name a code, and both are now driven behaviourally).
- `jcpe-fetq` still stands: four frozen quick-entry corpus cases assume a parse T0 does not produce.

## Exact commands and results (all after the last change)

- `/home/ubuntu/.bun/bin/bun --bun test` -> **2423 pass, 0 fail** across 223 files (698.63 s). Was 2399 across 221 at the last checkpoint.
- `bun scripts/run-playwright.ts test --project=chromium` -> **143 passed** (2.5 m)
- `bun scripts/run-playwright.ts test --project=firefox` -> **143 passed** (4.0 m)
- `bun scripts/run-playwright.ts test --project=webkit` -> **143 passed** (6.1 m) — WebKit had never run at all before this session
- `bun run verify:reproducible` -> pass — sha256 `fc3d63f7b601cd88cd676c055ae5577a2ae729e5d6560ed715ce9283ad36cd2f`, 798,140 bytes, rebuilt in isolated roots with differing mtimes
- `bun run typecheck` clean; `bun run lint` outcome pass (143 files, no findings).
- `bun scripts/verify-standalone.ts --static-only` -> pass, 0 findings; `bun run verify:licenses` -> pass (1 package, 1 asset).
- `bun scripts/validate-u1-contract.ts` -> pass, 0 findings, `mutationControlsReplayed: 32`.
- Artifact 798,140 bytes against the 1,048,576 shell ceiling.
- Matrix coverage, measured: 59 of 59 operation rows driven; 54 of 58 interaction cases; 46 of 46 quick-entry cases replayed; 18 of 18 laws on both polarities.
close_reason:
U1/verify complete. Every named gate is green from a clean invocation, with no skipped, retried, or quarantined check.

## Evidence, measured rather than declared

- **59 of 59 operation-matrix rows driven.** All 36 positive rows through the channel sweep; all 23 non-positive rows through `tests/integration/u1-edit-channel.test.ts` (11) and the new `tests/integration/u1-refusal-rows.test.ts` (12). Four of those rows turn out to have preconditions this surface cannot produce — U1-OPC-034, 035, 051, 052 — and each one's impossibility is *measured*, not asserted: the U1 selection bound is literally the document's chord capacity, `replace-document` is frozen outside the surface so document identity cannot move, the Delete gesture captures no revision to go stale, and a T0-refused draft is caught by a U1 pre-dispatch guard before any command is published.
- **54 of 58 interaction states driven**, by `tests/integration/u1-interaction-states.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/u1-pointer-listeners.spec.ts`, and `tests/e2e/u1-empty-errors.spec.ts`. The four remaining are blocked outside U1 and filed as `jcpe-bdga`: U1-INT-002/003/006 need playback, audition, or a moved playhead that only X0/X1 can supply, and U1-INT-026 needs a chart-region unmount the composition root never performs.
- **18 of 18 laws carry executed evidence on both polarities**, up from 10 when the ledger was first computed and 17 at the previous checkpoint. Every per-law floor in `PINNED_FLOOR` was raised to the measured value and `lawsWithBothPolarities` is pinned at 18, so coverage can rise but never fall.
- **46 of 46 quick-entry cases replayed** against the real controller, unchanged from the previous checkpoint.
- **The three-browser matrix runs for the first time.** WebKit could not launch on this host; the blocker was not only the `libicu74` Playwright names but also `libjxl.so.0.8` and `libbacktrace.so.0`, none of which exist in Ubuntu 25.10. Resolved with a verified sidecar extraction (Debian snapshot SHA-1 checked), not by relaxing anything.

## Six defects found and fixed, each with a regression test

1. Renaming the chart after any chord edit was refused with `command.logical_time_invalid` — the title command carried a private logical clock that started at zero and travelled backwards past the shared one. Every real session hits this.
2. A card unmounted mid-drag left the drag session set forever, so dragging was dead for the rest of the session.
3. The inline editors were unreachable from the keyboard in Chromium and Firefox (`autoFocus` is ignored on a dynamically inserted input), and cancelling one in WebKit dropped focus to the document body. The A0 focus-request renderer had the same gap after every command. Both are now layout effects that move focus explicitly and give the card back.
4. An overfilling duration notice stated no numbers; it now states the current fill, the resulting fill, and the capacity as exact rationals.
5. A declared short measure never showed its stored reason; the view model now carries it verbatim and the chart renders it in both views.
6. T0 diagnostic ranges were dropped at the token row; the code and its range are now both surfaced verbatim.

## Commands and results

- `/home/ubuntu/.bun/bin/bun --bun test` -> 2423 pass, 0 fail, 223 files (698.63 s).
- `bun scripts/run-playwright.ts test --project=chromium` -> 143 passed.
- `bun scripts/run-playwright.ts test --project=firefox` -> 143 passed.
- `bun scripts/run-playwright.ts test --project=webkit` -> 143 passed.
- `bun run verify:reproducible` -> pass, sha256 fc3d63f7b601cd88cd676c055ae5577a2ae729e5d6560ed715ce9283ad36cd2f, 798,140 bytes, isolated roots, differing mtimes.
- `bun scripts/verify-standalone.ts --static-only` -> pass, 0 findings. `bun run verify:licenses` -> pass.
- `bun scripts/validate-u1-contract.ts` -> pass, 0 findings, mutationControlsReplayed 32.
- `bun run typecheck` clean. `bun run lint` pass, 143 files, 0 findings.
- Artifact 798,140 bytes against the 1,048,576 shell ceiling.

## Carried forward, deliberately

`U1_EDITING_IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS` is now `"implemented-live"`. The fixture packet's four claim flags stay `false` because `scripts/validate-u1-contract.ts` hard-requires that and `tests/static/u1-contract.test.ts` proves it rejects a packet that sets them: they are the specification leaf's statement about itself. Moving them edits the independent oracle, which the sibling A0/U1 packet only did under a recorded human acceptance; none exists for U1. That decision is the user's, and it is the only thing between this leaf and a full production claim in the packet.

Open follow-ups: `jcpe-bdga` (four unreachable interaction cases, five declared refusal codes with no production site) and `jcpe-fetq` (four frozen corpus cases assuming a parse T0 does not produce).

title: A0/U1 amendment: atomic split-measure plan variant for overfill resolution
description:
Deferred by the U1/spec leaf (jcpe-milestone-reliable-studio-l3a.10.1) and recorded in docs/U1_EDITING_CONTRACT.md section 5.3 plus tests/fixtures/editing/u1-editing-contract.json handoff.deferredToDependentLeaves.

## Problem
REBUILD_PLAN 17.4 requires a duration edit that overfills a measure to offer 'Split at bar', 'Move following events', or 'Cancel'. Only the last two are expressible with one accepted A0 command today:
- Move following events = one 'move' command (targets = the overflow events, destination = the next measure, completionUpdates covering both measures).
- Split at bar would require inserting a new empty measure AND moving existing events into it while preserving their stable identities. That is two commands, so it cannot be one atomic, singly-undoable user action.

U1 v1 therefore states the overfill with its exact current fill, resulting fill, and bar capacity, and offers Move following events / Shorten the duration / Cancel. It never silently rebalances or drops beats. This is honest but incomplete against the plan text.

## Required work
Amend the A0/U1 atomic edit-plan contract (docs/A0_U1_ATOMIC_EDIT_PLAN_CONTRACT.md, src/application/application-edit-plan-contract.ts) with a sixth plan variant, provisionally 'split-measure': one source measure, one interior before-event boundary, exact rational partition of the measure total, stable identities preserved for every moved event, one fresh measure id, exact completion declarations for both resulting measures, its own refusal codes, bookmark mapping rows, and work counters. Then wire U1 operation U1-OP-013's sibling 'split-at-bar' row.

## Constraints
Same discipline as the accepted R1 packet: independently authored literal transitions, exact counters, undo/redo trios, collision and plus-one boundaries, mutation controls, and reciprocal trace/provenance links. The existing five plan kinds and the historical fifteen command kinds must not change. Do not weaken the one-command-per-gesture rule to work around the gap.

## Exit criteria
The amendment ships with its validator oracle, static test, production conformance witnesses, and a U1 operation row whose channel binding the U1 validator accepts.

title: Artifact byte budget: the studio shell is 7 KB from a ceiling that cannot be raised without the Atlas reservation
description:
## Finding
After U1/build increment 9 the generated artifact is 1,041,445 bytes against `foundationShellMaxBytes` = 1,048,576. That is 7,131 bytes of headroom.

## Why the ceiling cannot simply be raised
`scripts/validate-f0-contract.ts` requires:
- `maxUncompressedBytes` === 1,572,864 exactly;
- `foundationShellMaxBytes` > 0 and `reservedAtlasBytes` > 0;
- `foundationShellMaxBytes` + `reservedAtlasBytes` <= `maxUncompressedBytes`.

Today 1,048,576 + 524,288 = 1,572,864 exactly. The two values already saturate the budget, so every byte added to the shell ceiling must come out of the 512 KiB reserved for the reviewed Harmonic Atlas that D0 will fill. Raising the shell ceiling is therefore a real trade against a planned package, not a formality.

## Why this matters now
The 1 MiB shell ceiling was sized for the F0/U0 foundation. The artifact now also carries F1, F2, F3, T0, T1, V0, V1, V2, P0, C0, E0, E1, A0, A1, X0, X1 and U1. Still unshipped into the artifact: H0, G0-G9, U2-U11, D0 and D1. Roughly 7 KB cannot absorb the Musical Intelligence and Advanced Craft milestones, so the budget will bind long before the roadmap completes.

## The untaken lever
`scripts/build.ts` passes `--minify-whitespace` and `--minify-syntax` but NOT `--minify-identifiers`. Identifier mangling typically removes 20-30% of a bundle this shape, which would free far more than the current headroom. It was presumably left off for inspectability or CSP-hash stability; whichever it was is not recorded next to the flags.

## Decision this bead should produce
Choose explicitly, and record the reasoning in the F0 contract next to the flags:
1. enable `--minify-identifiers` and re-measure, or
2. re-split `foundationShellMaxBytes` against `reservedAtlasBytes` with D0's real content size in hand, or
3. raise `maxUncompressedBytes` above 1.5 MiB, which the validator currently pins exactly and which changes the published offline-artifact claim.

## Non-goals
Do not silently relax the ceiling to make one package fit. The point of the budget is that the artifact stays small enough to be a genuinely portable single file.

## Discovered by
Agent FoggyDeer while landing jcpe-milestone-reliable-studio-l3a.10.2 increment 9.
close_reason:
Resolved by enabling identifier minification, with the owner's explicit decision.

## What changed
scripts/build.ts now passes --minify-identifiers alongside --minify-whitespace and --minify-syntax. A rationale comment sits next to the flags.

## Measured effect
Artifact 1,041,445 -> 752,096 bytes. That is a 289,349-byte (27.8%) reduction and restores 296,480 bytes of headroom under the UNCHANGED 1,048,576-byte foundationShellMaxBytes. Neither foundationShellMaxBytes, reservedAtlasBytes (524,288) nor maxUncompressedBytes (1,572,864) moved, so the Atlas reservation D0 depends on is untouched. That is why this bead blocked D0 and why the block is now released without D0 paying for it.

## The policy this reversed, recorded honestly
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md previously stated: 'The identifier-preserving inspectable bundle policy is deliberate and unchanged.' This was a real documented policy, not an oversight, and it has been withdrawn rather than quietly contradicted. ARCHITECTURE.md now carries a section 'Identifier minification, and why the earlier policy was reversed' giving the measurement, what the reversal does not cost (reproducibility, the embedded CSP hashes, and manifest auditability) and what it does cost (reading the release bundle directly, which was never a release requirement).

## Gates proving nothing else moved
- bun run verify:reproducible -> pass, sha256 84ec86067127ee050cc6ff407aa080a6196bc4c85da7365dd8efe818d745560f, rebuilt in isolated roots with differing mtimes. Mangling is deterministic for a fixed input.
- bun run verify:standalone -> static inspection outcome pass; 24 browser cells passed, 12 failed. Every failure is WebKit, which cannot launch on this host for missing system libraries; Chromium and Firefox cells all pass. Before this change the same gate passed 12 and failed 24.
- bun scripts/run-playwright.ts test --project=chromium -> 105 passed. --project=firefox -> 105 passed.
- bun run typecheck clean; bun run lint outcome pass, 0 findings.

## Options not taken, and why
Re-splitting foundationShellMaxBytes against reservedAtlasBytes would have spent a budget for D0 before anyone measured D0's real Atlas size. Raising maxUncompressedBytes above 1.5 MiB would have changed the published offline-artifact claim and is pinned exactly by validate-f0-contract.ts. Minification cost neither.

## Left for later
The three remaining decision inputs in this bead's description are now moot for the current milestone, but the underlying arithmetic still holds: foundationShellMaxBytes + reservedAtlasBytes still equals maxUncompressedBytes exactly, so a FUTURE shell increase still has to come out of the Atlas reservation. The headroom bought here is roughly 296 KB, not unlimited.

title: U1 spec packet: four quick-entry corpus cases disagree with the T0 grammar they assume
notes:
Found by the U1 verify leaf (jcpe-milestone-reliable-studio-l3a.10.3) while replaying the byte-pinned corpus `tests/fixtures/editing/quick-entry-cases.json` against the real controller. The corpus sets `t0ResultIsScenarioInput: true`, so each case's `t0Result` is an assumption; these four cases assume a parse the real T0 grammar does not produce, which leaves their declared U1 classification describing a parse that never happens.

1. U1-QE-046 transposes the annotation and the duration. The case writes `| Cmaj7 "head in":4 |` and expects a parsed draft. The T0 grammar carries an event annotation after the duration: `| Cmaj7:4 "head in" |` parses with annotation="head in", while the case's own text is refused as chart.unsupported_notation. The case note ("an event annotation is inert data carried through unchanged") states the right intent; only the draft text is wrong.

2. U1-QE-030 contradicts U1-QE-013. It assumes `| C:4 | | ` is refused with chart.unsupported_notation; U1-QE-013 states that two adjacent boundary tokens deliberately enclose one empty measure, and T0 accepts the draft.

3. U1-QE-033 contradicts U1-QE-006. It assumes `| C |` is refused with chart.layout_invalid; U1-QE-006 states that T0 allocates the whole bar to the single undurated slot, and T0 accepts the draft.

4. U1-QE-026, U1-QE-027 and U1-QE-036 under-state T0's recovery set: T0 recovers one chord after a forbidden fragment header, two chords from `| C:4 | D`, and every chord of the overfilled bar, where the cases assume none, one and none.

Separately, `tokenStates` is authored per case with no stated total projection, and two pairs cannot be reconciled by any single rule over the declared T0 result: U1-QE-021 (two recovered chords, one non-fill diagnostic, no invalid row) against U1-QE-030 (one recovered chord, one non-fill diagnostic, one invalid row); and U1-QE-036 (one invalid row for four hundred unrecovered chords) against U1-QE-025 (one invalid row for one). The verify leaf asserts only the projection law U1 owns and leaves the invalid-row rule to the packet.

Nothing here changes production behaviour: the U1 classification laws hold against the real parse in every case, and the conformance replay asserts them. What is needed is a packet decision — re-pin the affected cases against the real grammar, or state why the assumed outcomes are correct and T0 must change. The divergences are named in T0_SCENARIO_DIVERGENCES in tests/conformance/u1-production-conformance.test.ts so a fifth one cannot appear unnoticed.
close_reason:
Resolved as a packet correction: the corpus was wrong, T0 was right, and the divergence list is now empty.

## How each answer was derived

Not from the parser. Every replacement value comes from `docs/T0_SYNTAX_CONTRACT.md` plus the independently authored T0 packet `tests/fixtures/theory/chart-cases.json`, which pins the same shapes:

- `T0-CHART-ERR-007` (`@meter 4/4\nC`) declares `insertableCount: 1` — the fragment header refuses the draft and T0 still publishes the chord after the LF.
- `T0-CHART-ERR-013` (`| C:4`) declares `insertableCount: 1` for an unclosed measure.
- `T0-CHART-ERR-019` (`| C:3 Dm:2 |`) declares `insertableDurations: ["explicit:3/1", "explicit:2/1"]` — **every** chord of an overfilled bar is recovered, not none.
- `T0-CHART-ERR-031` (`C | D:4 |`) declares the mixed pair literally: the undurated chord as `duration.kind: requires-caller` with reason `chart.layout_invalid`, the durated one as resolved.
- Contract 5.2 orders the event as `chord-symbol duration? (hspace json-string)?` and states that two adjacent boundary tokens enclose an empty measure; 5.7 step 5 divides the whole bar among undurated slots; 5.8 resumes recovery after an explicit LF.

## The six cases

| Case | What was wrong | Correction |
|---|---|---|
| U1-QE-026 | declared no recovery after `chart.header_forbidden_in_fragment` | publishes `C` (resolved 4/1), per 5.8 and T0-CHART-ERR-007 |
| U1-QE-027 | declared one recovered chord for `\| C:4 \| D` | publishes both: `C` resolved, `D` requires-caller |
| U1-QE-030 | declared `\| C:4 \| \| ` refused, contradicting its own sibling U1-QE-013 | restated as the positive it is — a barred sequence whose last measure is empty parses, and the empty final measure is carried into the section rather than dropped or joined. Draft text untouched. |
| U1-QE-033 | the draft `\| C \|` cannot produce the `requires-caller` recovery the case is *for*: 5.7 allocates the whole bar, exactly as U1-QE-006 states | draft corrected to `C \| D:4 \|`, the shape T0-CHART-ERR-031 pins. The case keeps its declared expectation, its kind, and its law links. |
| U1-QE-036 | declared no recovery from the overfilled bar | publishes all 1,024 chords, per T0-CHART-ERR-019; `canInsertOneChord` becomes true because one recovered chord fits the empty destination |
| U1-QE-046 | the draft wrote the annotation before the duration | draft corrected to `\| Cmaj7:4 "head in" \|`; the case's own note already stated the right intent |

Only two drafts changed, and in both the draft is what contradicted the published grammar. Four cases kept their pinned input and had their declared T0 result corrected.

## The unstated projection, now stated and enforced

The separate half of this bug was that `tokenStates` was authored per case with no total rule, so two pairs could not be reconciled. The rule production actually holds is one line of `StudioQuickEntryToken`'s own contract: a refused draft yields one `insertable` row per recovered chord **plus one `invalid` row per T0 diagnostic**. Under it, eight further cases were short a row — U1-QE-021, 023, 024, 031, 032, 034 and 035 alongside the six above — and none of those eight had been noticed, because the replay was only counting insertable rows.

- The corpus now states it in `classificationPolicy.tokenStateProjection` (parsed / refused / unparsed / truncation).
- `scripts/validate-u1-contract.ts` recomputes the whole ordered sequence per case and compares element by element, and separately requires the projection statement to be present and unrestated. Counting insertable rows alone let a case drop its diagnostic rows silently; that hole is closed.
- `docs/U1_EDITING_CONTRACT.md` section 4 states the projection normatively.

## Evidence

- `bun scripts/validate-u1-contract.ts` — outcome **pass**, 0 findings, 32 of 32 mutation controls replayed, with no `--allow-pending-freeze`.
- `tests/conformance/u1-production-conformance.test.ts` — `T0_SCENARIO_DIVERGENCES` and `BLOCKED_REASON_BY_STATEMENT` are deleted, and the weakened token assertion is replaced by an exact `toEqual` for every case. 47/47 pass. A future case built on an impossible parse now fails instead of being excused.
- All 46 cases were independently replayed against the real controller through the real F2/F3 boundary: 0 of 46 disagree on any of the 12 compared fields or on token rows.
